explanation: Dense copy-phase feature: 99.9% of activation mass is in the copy phase (t > L; essentially silent in the original phase and at the <DEL> step), active on ~41% of copy steps. Within the copy phase, firing rate and magnitude are graded by the identity of the token being output: highest when outputting t (85% active, 22% of mass) or j (83%), then z, e, c, p (~65-68%), g, y, o, s, 1, u (~40-55%), and lower for other tokens. Activation also rises when the NEXT output is t or j, so it ramps up in the step before a t is emitted. The largest activations (max ~5) occur when outputting t inside runs of repeated t (e.g. ...v t t... copying), peaking at the first t-to-t output. Not driven by L, digits count, or in_count. A token-set predicate captures ~87% of mass but precision is only ~0.67, because the feature fires weakly on many other copy-phase outputs; it behaves like a graded token-preference over output identity rather than a crisp detector.
